question: A charity is designing a way of working in which Claude drafts its monthly supporter update. Which sequence of steps is correct?
options: A) Draft one past month with Claude; agree what a good update contains; have the editor mark what is wrong; change one thing and try again
B) Draft one past month with Claude; have the editor mark what is wrong; change one thing and try again; agree what a good update contains
C) Agree what a good update contains; draft one past month with Claude; have the editor mark what is wrong; change one thing and try again
D) Agree what a good update contains; have the editor mark what is wrong; draft one past month with Claude; change one thing and try again
correct_answers: C) Agree what a good update contains; draft one past month with Claude; have the editor mark what is wrong; change one thing and try again
explanations: Drafting before agreeing the standard means the editor's marks are personal preference, and the design converges on one person's taste.
Leaving the definition of a good update until last means the first three steps were judged against nobody's stated standard.
Correct. Agree the standard, produce a draft on a known month, have it marked against that standard, then change one thing at a time. Each round then tells you something you can act on.
Marking what is wrong before anything has been drafted is impossible; there is no draft to mark.
